title: Bilateral Dependency Optimization: Defending Against Model-inversion Attacks

problem.claim: Model-inversion attacks can recover training data from a well-trained classifier, causing privacy leakage.

gap.claim: Unilateral dependency minimization conflicts with supervised-loss minimization, creating a trade-off between model-inversion robustness and classification utility.

contributions.claim: Introduces bilateral dependency optimization, minimizing dependency between latent representations and inputs while maximizing dependency between latent representations and outputs.
Formulates dependency constraints as a generally applicable regularizer alongside standard deep-neural-network losses, with dependency criteria chosen for different tasks.
Provides two implementations using constrained covariance and the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize BiDO as a novel road for defending against model-inversion attacks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: BiDO achieves state-of-the-art defense performance across various datasets, classifiers, and model-inversion attacks.
BiDO incurs a minor classification-accuracy drop relative to an undefended well-trained classifier.

narrative_sequence.summary: Model-inversion attacks threaten training-data privacy by recovering data from classifiers.
Prior defenses minimize dependency between classifier inputs and outputs.
This unilateral strategy conflicts with supervised learning and creates a robustness–utility trade-off.
BiDO balances input disentanglement and output predictiveness through bilateral dependency optimization and regularization.
Two dependency-based implementations are evaluated and reported to provide strong defense with a minor accuracy cost.

source_observation.claim: The method reduces dependency between latent representations and inputs while increasing dependency between latent representations and outputs.

interpretation.claim: Privacy objectives can be aligned with task utility by constraining different representation relationships rather than suppressing input–output dependence globally.

application.claim: When privacy and prediction objectives conflict, consider representation-level regularization that separates nuisance information from task-relevant information.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy generalizes beyond the reported model-inversion defense setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, classifiers, attack configurations, dependency-criterion details, or quantitative accuracy and defense results.
The abstract does not provide implementation, training, or reproducibility details.
